verdict.rationale: Homebrew's own `brew tap` command can add third-party repositories from any Git URL, and a community report confirms people self-host taps on their own git servers. That covers the 'point at private registries' part of the story. Nothing in the evidence documents scoped credentials or authentication for those sources, and no bottle or registry mirror configuration is shown; tap trust scoping is about which items to trust, not about authentication. Missing for 10: documented scoped or per-source authentication, mirror or alternate bottle-domain configuration, and first-party guidance on private tap authentication.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can point the manager at private registries or mirrors with scoped authentication

citations.quote: The `brew tap` command adds repositories that Homebrew can use for formulae, casks and external commands.
the two-argument form accepts any URL supported by Git.
Your server must implement the git protocol, so you can't just put it behind a CDN; you need to run and fortify a git server.
